articles.body:
[q="wtcannonjr"]We assumed the turn 6 Confluence Phase ends after Share Technologies step since the Player Aid said No Bid step.

So the correct sequence is to play all steps of Turn 6 except the bid steps for Colonies and Research Teams?[/q]

I just found this quote from the designer in another folder.

[q="TauCetiDD"] So, the final “Scoring-Only Economy Phase” is just a normal economy phase. Turn 6 goes as follows:

Trade Phase: players invent the last technologies for the game. Trading is dominated by getting the resources to invent those technologies. Converters that produce victory points are also pretty valuable, whereas converters that just produce resources are worth comparably little (but not nothing).

“Scoring-Only” Economy Phase: this is the last economy phase of the game, and has almost no special rules. Players run what economy they can, producing victory points and some resources. The only thing that makes this phase different than other economy phases is that it's OK to produce the wrong colors of resources, so long as the sizes are correct. You won't be able to use the resources to do anything (other than end-game scoring, which doesn't care about resource color), so the resource colors don't really matter anymore. 

Note that you do still need the correct colors of input resources.

Oh, and as your reminded me, player keep their own donation goods (since there isn't another trade phase to trade them away).

Confluence Phase: get victory points for sharing technologies, and then the game ends (before bidding starts). During the end of the game, leftover resources are turned into victory points at a terrible rate.

<=oOo=>[/q]

articles.body:
The official answer from me is, yes, the Zeth get to steal on the last turn of the game.  It's the final thing that happens before counting score.

In practice, end-game theft makes the target lose half a point, and the Zeth gain somewhat less than that, so it has very little impact.

There's an issue: Zeth stealing breaks the rule that the color of resources doesn't matter on the last turn of the game.  Thankfully, it works fine for everyone other than the Zeth, but the Zeth shouldn't run a stealing converter if they wouldn't have the correct colors.  That said, those “correct colors” are usually black, and the Zeth generally produce huge piles of that, so in practice it's usually fine.

That said, I wouldn't bother giving the Zeth more than a ship or (at most) two for safety on the final turn.

Due to the minor impact of stealing on the last turn, you could house-rule it either way.  I prefer to let the Zeth steal, as otherwise their special power has become completely useless on the final turn, so it's more fun for the Zeth.

articles.body: Good to know.  In terms of very little impact, we played a very close game last night where the 1st 5 places were only separated by a margin of 2.5 points.  So a turn 6 Zeth steal may have altered the results (alas, probably not enough for me playing the Zeth to "steal" a victory).
